data.name: Privacy_FilterEnabled_Description
data.value: When enabled, only messages from whitelisted channels are persisted to the database. Disabling restores upstream ChatTwo behavior (everything except battle messages is stored).

data.name: Privacy_FilterEnabled_StorageOnly_Help
data.value: The filter only controls what is written to the local database. The chat log itself keeps showing every message live, disallowed channels just stop being saved. Use the channel hide options in your in-game chat tabs if you want to remove channels from the visible chat.

data.name: Privacy_Whitelist_Help
data.value: Pick which channels are stored in the local database. Privacy-First default: only your own conversations. Use the buttons below to apply a preset.

data.name: Privacy_PersistUnknown_Description
data.value: Failsafe for ChatTypes added by future FFXIV patches that this plugin does not yet know about. Default OFF (Privacy-First). Turn ON if you want a complete log including future channels.

data.name: Cleanup_Help_Intro
data.value: The privacy filter only applies to new messages. Use the cleanup below to retroactively remove already-stored messages that don't match your saved whitelist.

data.name: Cleanup_Help_SavedNote
data.value: Cleanup uses your SAVED whitelist (Plugin.Config), not unsaved edits above. Click Save first if you want to apply your current edits.

data.name: Retention_Help_SavedNote
data.value: The manual sweep uses your SAVED retention policy, not the slider values above. Click Save first if you want the run to apply your current edits.

data.name: Cleanup_Preview_Stale
data.value: Preview is out of date — your whitelist has changed since the last refresh. Click Refresh to recalculate.

data.name: Cleanup_NoPreview
data.value: No preview yet. Click Refresh to compute the impact.

data.name: Cleanup_Apply_Tooltip
data.value: Ctrl+Shift: Hard-deletes {0:N0} messages, then runs VACUUM. Cannot be undone.

data.name: Cleanup_PreviewError
data.value: Failed to compute cleanup preview, see /xllog

data.name: Retention_Enabled_Name
data.value: Auto-delete messages after a per-channel retention window

data.name: Retention_Enabled_Description
data.value: When enabled, messages older than the configured window are deleted on every plugin start (at most once per 24 hours). Off by default. The plugin never deletes history without your explicit consent.

data.name: Retention_Default_Help
data.value: Applies to channels without an explicit override below.

data.name: Retention_Apply_Tooltip
data.value: Ctrl+Shift: runs the retention sweep immediately using the SAVED policy. Save your changes first.

data.name: Wizard_Intro
data.value: Pick a starting profile. You can change anything later under Settings → Privacy.

data.name: Wizard_Profile_PrivacyFirst_Description
data.value: Only your own conversations are stored: Tells, Party, FC, Linkshells, Cross-World Linkshells, Alliance and ExtraChat. Public chat, NPC dialogue and system spam are dropped at the storage layer. Retention follows the spec defaults (Tells 365 days, own-conversation channels 90 days).

data.name: Wizard_Profile_Casual_Description
data.value: Privacy-First plus a 24-hour window for public chat (Say, Shout, Yell, both emote types, Novice Network). For RP players who want to look up the last scene without keeping public chat forever.

data.name: Wizard_Profile_FullHistory_Description
data.value: Disables the privacy filter entirely. Stores everything except battle logs, just like upstream Chat 2. Retention is OFF, history grows forever.

data.name: Wizard_Profile_FullHistory_GdprWarning
data.value: GDPR notice: storing third-party messages (Say/Shout/Yell of strangers, NPC dialogue with player names, etc.) for an unlimited time may exceed the personal/household exemption (Art. 2(2)(c)). Use this profile only if you have a clear reason to keep the full archive.

data.name: Export_Help
data.value: Export stored messages to Markdown, JSON or CSV. Use this to fulfil a request for access from someone whose messages you have, or to take your own history with you.

data.name: Export_Empty
data.value: Export complete: no messages matched the filter.

data.name: Theme_Enabled_Name
data.value: Use the Hellion theme across all plugin windows

data.name: Theme_Enabled_Description
data.value: Hellion Online Media palette of Arctic Cyan plus Ember Orange, applied across the chat log, settings, viewers and the wizard. Disable to fall back to the default Dalamud look.

data.name: Theme_WindowOpacity_Help
data.value: How opaque the plugin panes are. Lower values let the game shine through; form fields and dialogs stay opaque on top so they remain readable.

data.name: Theme_UseHellionFont_Description
data.value: Renders chat and UI in Exo 2 (SIL Open Font License 1.1) which ships with the plugin. Disable to fall back to whatever font you picked under Settings → Fonts.

data.name: About_Maintainer_Body
data.value: I maintain Hellion Chat through Hellion Online Media. The website has the contact details for licensing, legal or business questions.

data.name: About_Mission_P1
data.value: Hellion Chat is not trying to replace Chat 2. Chat 2 ships a complete chat experience with full history available for filtering, search and replay. That default is the right one for most users. This fork takes a different stance: a smaller default footprint, with extra knobs for users who want to keep less third-party chat on disk.

data.name: About_Mission_P2
data.value: The reason I wanted that narrower default was personal. After two years on Chat 2 my database had grown past two million messages, most of them /say, /shout and /yell from strangers in Limsa. That data is exactly what makes Chat 2's full-history view powerful and most users are happy to keep it. For my own taste I wanted a smaller default. So I built this fork.

data.name: About_Mission_P3
data.value: I am not chasing a big audience and the fork is not in competition with Chat 2. The code is open under the same EUPL-1.2 licence as the upstream plugin. Infi, Anna or anyone else are welcome to read it, borrow ideas, ask questions, or ignore the project. All three are fine by me.

data.name: About_BuiltOn_P1
data.value: Hellion Chat is a fork of Chat 2 by Infi and Anna (ascclemens). The chat replacement window, the IPC integration, the rendering engine and the entire storage core come from upstream Chat 2.

data.name: About_BuiltOn_P2
data.value: The webinterface is the only major piece I removed. It is built for remote access to chat from a second device, which is a different focus than the smaller default footprint this fork is built around. Aligning it with these defaults would have meant a substantial rebuild, so removing it was the cleaner path for this particular fork.

data.name: About_License_P1
data.value: Hellion Chat and Chat 2 both ship under the European Union Public Licence v1.2 (EUPL-1.2).

data.name: AutoTellTabs_GreetedTooltip
data.value: Marked as greeted. Click to remove the marker.

data.name: ChatLog_AutoTellTabs_Enable_Name
data.value: Open a tab automatically for each tell partner

data.name: ChatLog_AutoTellTabs_Enable_Description
data.value: When you receive or send a /tell, a temporary tab dedicated to that player is opened automatically. Tabs vanish on logout.

data.name: ChatLog_AutoTellTabs_Limit_Name
data.value: Maximum number of auto tell tabs

data.name: ChatLog_AutoTellTabs_Limit_Description
data.value: When the limit is reached, greeted tabs with the oldest activity are dropped first. The change applies on the next /tell.

data.name: ChatLog_AutoTellTabs_Compact_Description
data.value: Show only a thin separator between persistent tabs and auto tell tabs, without the section header.

data.name: ChatLog_AutoTellTabs_GreetedToggle_Description
data.value: Adds a click-to-toggle button next to each auto tell tab to mark a partner as already greeted, dimming the tab name when set. Useful for club greeters tracking many parallel conversations; off by default.

data.name: ChatLog_AutoTellTabs_PreloadHint
data.value: The number of preloaded tells is configured in the Privacy tab.

data.name: ChatLog_AutoTellTabs_ConflictHint
data.value: Heads-up: if XIV Messanger or a similar plugin is suppressing direct messages, turn its "Suppress DMs" option off so Hellion Chat can receive tells and open the auto tabs.

data.name: Privacy_AutoTellTabs_Preload_Description
data.value: How many earlier tell messages are loaded from the database when an auto tell tab is opened. 0 disables the preload.

data.name: Privacy_AutoTellTabs_Preload_Hint
data.value: Only takes effect when auto tell tabs are enabled in the Chat tab.

data.name: SettingsRefactor_Migration_Content
data.value: Hellion Chat 0.5.0 reorganised the settings into themed tabs. Your chat database and your message history stay untouched. Settings have been reset to defaults; if you want to pick a privacy profile again, the reopen button is in the Privacy tab. A backup of your previous config is at HellionChat.json.pre-v10-backup next to the live config file.

data.name: Tabs_Presets_Linkshell_Hint
data.value: If you use multiple linkshells, the maintainer recommends one tab per shell for cleaner readability. Duplicate this tab and narrow the channel selection per copy.

data.name: Settings_Appearance_Colours_PresetsHint
data.value: Tip: presets overwrite your current channel colours immediately.

data.name: Settings_Window_PopOutInputEnabled_Description
data.value: Master switch: lets you type and send messages directly inside every pop-out window (including auto-tell tabs). Channel changes inside a pop-out apply globally just like in the main window; the text buffer and history cursor stay independent per pop-out.

data.name: Popout_v060_HintText
data.value: New in v0.6.0: you can type directly inside pop-out windows. Toggle the master switch in the window settings to enable it.
